summary: Canada admits visa-exempt nationals arriving by air with an eTA (CAD 7, valid up to 5 years), lets US citizens enter with no eTA or visa at all, and requires everyone else to obtain a visitor visa (TRV, CAD 100) — visitors are normally allowed to stay up to 6 months.

VA.notes: eTA (CAD 7, valid up to 5 years) required when flying to Canada; arriving by land or sea from the US needs only your passport. Stays of up to 6 months are normally granted.

conditionalWaivers.text: Citizens of the countries in Canada's expanded eTA program — Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Brazil, Costa Rica, Mexico, Morocco, Panama, the Philippines, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Seychelles, Thailand, Trinidad and Tobago and Uruguay — qualify for the CAD 7 eTA instead of a visitor visa if they hold a valid US nonimmigrant visa (or held a Canadian visa in the past 10 years) and are flying to Canada. No other nationality can substitute a US visa for a Canadian one.

fee.notes: Payable online by card. Required only when flying to or transiting through a Canadian airport; not needed for land or sea arrivals.
Plus CAD 85 biometrics fee for most applicants. Applications are made online; processing times vary widely by country.

source.name: IRCC — Apply for a visitor visa

fee.notes: Requires a letter of acceptance from a designated learning institution and, for most students, a provincial attestation letter. Biometrics CAD 85 extra.
Most streams require a job offer and, often, an LMIA from the employer. Open work permits carry an additional CAD 100 fee.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for the duration of your intended stay in Canada. There is no additional 6-month requirement.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but healthcare for visitors is expensive and public coverage does not apply — comprehensive medical coverage is strongly recommended.

onwardTicket.text: Not a formal requirement, but border services officers may ask how and when you will leave Canada — a return or onward ticket makes admission smoother.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is set, but officers may ask you to show you have enough money for your stay, along with ties to your home country.

currencyLimits.text: Currency and monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared to CBSA on arrival and departure. There is no limit on the amount — only a reporting duty.

notes: Declare all food, plants and animal products — undeclared items carry steep on-the-spot fines.
Cannabis is legal inside Canada but taking it across the border in either direction is a serious criminal offense.
Firearms must be declared in writing at the border; most handguns are prohibited.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments (including Interac debit) are accepted virtually everywhere; cash is rarely needed. Tipping 15–20% is customary in restaurants, and displayed prices exclude sales tax.

safety.text: Canada is one of the safest countries in the world for visitors, with low crime nationwide. Take normal precautions in big-city downtown areas at night, and prepare properly for winter driving and remote wilderness travel.

bestTimeToVisit.text: June to September offers warm weather for cities, lakes and the Rockies; December to March is the season for skiing, winter festivals and northern lights.

idp.text: Canada is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Canada is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Canada yet.

tips.text: Apply for the eTA only at canada.ca. It costs CAD 7. Lookalike third-party sites charge many times that for the same 5-minute application, and some are outright scams.
The eTA is only for air travel. If you drive or sail in from the US, visa-exempt visitors need only their passport. No eTA, no fee.
US land border crossings can back up for hours at peak times. Check CBSA's published border wait times and consider quieter crossings or off-peak hours.
Never take cannabis across the Canadian border in either direction. It is a criminal offense even though cannabis is legal within Canada and in some US states.

faq.question: Do US citizens need an eTA or visa for Canada?
faq.answer: No. US citizens are exempt from both the eTA and the visitor visa. A valid US passport is enough, by air or land, for visits of up to 6 months.

faq.question: What is the Canadian eTA and how much does it cost?
faq.answer: The Electronic Travel Authorization is an online entry requirement for visa-exempt travelers flying to Canada. It costs CAD 7, is usually approved within minutes, and stays valid for up to 5 years or until your passport expires. Apply only at canada.ca.

faq.question: Do Mexican citizens need a visa for Canada?
faq.answer: It depends. Since February 29, 2024, Mexicans qualify for the eTA (air travel only) if they have held a Canadian visa in the past 10 years or hold a valid US non-immigrant visa. Otherwise they must apply for a visitor visa (TRV, CAD 100).

faq.question: How long can I stay in Canada as a visitor?
faq.answer: Most visitors are allowed up to 6 months. The officer may stamp a different date; if there is no handwritten date, the default is 6 months from entry. You can apply online for a visitor record to extend your stay before it expires.

faq.question: Do I need an eTA if I enter Canada by car from the US?
faq.answer: No. The eTA applies only to arrivals by air. Visa-exempt travelers crossing by land or sea just need a valid passport; travelers from visa-required countries need a visitor visa regardless of how they arrive.
